b: In a warp away from the usual album, book or film, this month author Michael Smith peers into the dodecahedron of his mind to consider the geometry of the cosmos, time, and reality itself

Leonardo da Vinci drew the dodecahedron above as an illustration for Da Divina Proportione, a mathematical treatise written by his pal, the Franciscan friar and geometrician Luca Pacioli. The book had a deep influence on the development of the Italian Renaissance when it was published in Venice in 1509, diffusing what was a very learned and esoteric subject matter into the fields of painting, sculpture, architecture and music.
